findings.comment: Drivable surfaces within electric easements are not specified on the grading plan. The plan shows easement boundaries but provides no notes indicating whether surfaces will be paved (HMAC or PCC), grass, gravel, or other materials. Please add notes to the grading plan (Sheet 11) specifying that all-weather surfaces (hot mix asphalt concrete or Portland cement concrete) capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight will be provided within all electric easement areas to accommodate maintenance vehicles.
applicableAreas: All electric easement areas on site
findings.observation: Examined the grading plan (Sheet 11) for surface type specifications within electric easement areas. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 explicitly confirmed: 'There are **no notes or specifications** on this sheet that indicate the surface type (paved, grass, gravel, etc.) within the electric easement areas or general utility easement areas.' The grading plan shows easement boundaries with dashed lines and labels, but the legend does not include an easement representation key, and no detail notes or specifications indicate whether easement areas will be paved (HMAC or PCC), grass, gravel, or other surface type. The contour lines shown crossing through easement areas do not indicate any special treatment or surface specification—they simply follow the general site drainage pattern.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires all-weather drivable surfaces capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs rear axle) for maintenance truck access. LDC § 25-12-173 Section 202.1 defines 'All Weather Driving Surface' as HMAC or Portland cement concrete pavement. The grouping guidance identifies 'Grading plan or civil notes indicate electric easement will have grass or gravel surface instead of paved' as a common violation. The applicant has a duty to affirmatively specify that easement surfaces will be paved. The absence of any surface specification for the easement areas means it is not clear that the applicant intends to provide paved (HMAC or PCC) surfaces. This is particularly critical for distribution easements that must accommodate Austin Energy maintenance trucks. The grading plan must explicitly specify the surface material for all electric easement areas.

findings.comment: Drivable surfaces within electric easements are not labeled or specified. Provide explicit surface material specifications (HMAC or PCC pavement) for all electric easement areas on the grading plan and construction details, demonstrating that surfaces are capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight and 32,530 lbs rear axle weight. If any electric easement areas are not paved all-weather surfaces, revise grading/landscaping to provide such surfaces or provide written approval from Austin Energy for alternative surface treatment.
applicableAreas: All electric easement areas shown on grading plan
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) delineates easement boundaries (5' Electric Easements, 5' P.U.E., 25' Drainage Easement, etc.) but provides NO explicit surface material specifications (HMAC pavement, PCC concrete, gravel, grass, or unpaved) within the electric easement areas. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 confirms: 'There are very few explicit surface material specifications written directly within the easement areas...surfaces are largely indicated by functional line work and symbols rather than distinct material hatching...general grass, gravel, or asphalt specifications are not explicitly labeled within the utility or drainage easements.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) notes that transformer pads are 'located in spaces containing overlapping circular symbols indicating tree canopies, suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas, though the exact surface material is not named.' The grading plan legend does not include symbols for surface finish types (grass hatch, gravel hatch, asphalt hatch) that would enable identification of easement surface treatment. The plan shows contours and drainage features within easements but not surface material specifications.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that drivable surfaces within electric easements be suitable for maintenance vehicles and large bucket trucks. LDC § 25-12-173 Section 202.1 defines 'all-weather driving surface' as Hot Mix Asphaltic Concrete (HMAC) or Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavement capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight. Grass, gravel, and unpaved surfaces do not qualify. The grading plan is the appropriate sheet to specify these surface materials, but it lacks explicit callouts. While driveways and parking areas shown in the western portion of the site are clearly delineated as paved (implied by curb lines and pavement specifications in construction details), the eastern and southern electric easement areas are not similarly labeled. The absence of explicit surface specification prevents verification of compliance. This creates genuine ambiguity—the surfaces may be paved (meeting code) or unpaved (failing code), but cannot be determined from the submitted plans.

findings.comment: Drivable surfaces within electric easements not suitable for maintenance vehicles and large bucket trucks; surfaces are unpaved, grass, gravel, or otherwise inadequate for heavy equipment. No surface material specification is provided for the 5-foot electric easements. Specify that all electric easement areas shall be graded and paved with HMAC or PCC concrete capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight. Provide a grading and paving plan for all electric easement access routes, showing the surface specification and confirming that maintenance vehicle access is maintained along the full length of easements.
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas, particularly the 5-foot electric easements along eastern and southeastern property boundaries
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Grading Plan (Sheet 11) reveals that surface materials within electric easement areas are NOT explicitly specified or called out. The plan shows contour lines and spot elevations within the '5' Electric Easement' along the eastern boundary and the '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement' in the southeast corner, but no hatching, notation, or legend entry indicates whether these areas will be paved with HMAC or PCC concrete, or left unpaved (grass, gravel, or dirt). The Legend on Sheet 11 does not include surface material specifications for easement areas. The General Notes do not address surface specifications for electric easement areas. Vision analysis of electrical and site plans shows that existing trees and a wood fence occupy areas adjacent to or potentially within the easement boundaries, but there is no indication that maintenance vehicle access routes have been graded and paved.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 explicitly requires 'all-weather surface definition: Hot mix asphaltic concrete (HMAC) or Portland cement concrete (PCC) pavement capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with maximum 32,530 lbs rear axle weight. Gravel, grass, and unpaved surfaces do NOT qualify.' LDC § 25-12-173 Section 202.1 defines an all-weather driving surface for maintenance access. The applicant must specify paved surfaces (HMAC or PCC) in all areas designated as electric easement or maintenance access corridors. Without this specification, there is no assurance that maintenance trucks and bucket trucks can access the easement. The narrow 5-foot easements with existing trees and fencing suggest that maintenance access has not been adequately planned.

findings.comment: 24/7 truck access to transformer locations is not shown or dimensioned. Four transformer pads are depicted on the electrical design plan and shown adjacent to internal driveways, but no dimensions confirm that pads are within 6 feet of a drivable surface per UCM § 1.10.4. Please dimension the distance from each transformer pad to the nearest drivable surface (parking area or driveway) and confirm that all transformers are located within 6 feet of a paved surface capable of supporting truck access.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) for transformer pad locations and access specifications. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Four transformers are shown, all exactly labeled **"Electrical Transformer Pad".** They are located at: West side adjacent to Building 2; Southwest side adjacent to Building 8 (located within a dashed "Vault Easement"); Center between Buildings 4 and 5; Center-South between Buildings 6 and 7. **Dimensions/Access**: The transformer pads are drawn as graphical rectangles, but no specific pad dimensions (e.g., 10'x10') are provided. There are no designated, dimensioned, or specially paved "access routes" explicitly labeled for utility vehicles to reach these pads, though they are all located directly adjacent to the site's main internal driveways/parking areas.' No dimensions from transformer pads to drivable surfaces are provided. No note specifies that pads are within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires 24/7 truck access to all Austin Energy facilities. UCM § 1.10.4 specifies that 'Equipment pads [must be] Within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility.' This is a specific measurement requirement—not a general recommendation. The grouping guidance identifies 'Transformer access deficiency: Utility plan shows pad-mounted transformer location but no dimensioned access route from parking area, or transformer located more than 6 feet from drivable surface without demonstrating adequate truck access' as a common violation pattern. The site plan shows transformers in general proximity to driveways but provides NO dimensions confirming that pads are within the required 6-foot distance from drivable surfaces. Without these dimensions, compliance cannot be verified.

findings.comment: 24/7 truck access to transformer pad locations is not clearly shown or dimensioned on plans. Provide dimension callouts from each of the four transformer pad locations to the nearest accessible parking or traffic area, demonstrating that all transformers are within 6 feet of all-weather drivable surface suitable for bucket truck access per UCM § 1.10.4. If any transformer is more than 6 feet from accessible parking/traffic area, relocate or provide written approval from Austin Energy demonstrating acceptable maintenance access methodology.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations shown on electrical design plan and site plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identifies four transformer pads located at: (1) west side of Bldg. 1; (2) west side of Bldg. 2; (3) east side of Bldg. 4; (4) east side of Bldg. 6 (between Bldg 6 & 7). Vision analysis of Sheet 21 notes: 'Transformer Pad (Typ.) is explicitly labeled on the west side of the property near Bldg 1 and Bldg 2...located immediately adjacent to the main western driveway entrance loop...highly accessible from the vehicular parking areas.' However, the transformer pads on the east side (near Bldgs 4 and 6) are shown 'located in spaces containing overlapping circular symbols indicating tree canopies, suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas.' Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows no specific callouts or dimension lines indicating the distance from transformer pad locations to accessible parking/traffic areas. The plan shows landscaped areas around these eastern transformer locations but does not provide measurements demonstrating the 6-foot maximum distance to parking/traffic areas required by the grouping.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 and § 1.10.4 require that equipment pads (transformer pads) be within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility. The grouping specifies: 'Equipment pads: Within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility.' One transformer pad is clearly accessible (west side, adjacent to main driveway). However, the two transformer pads located on the east side of the property (near Buildings 4 and 6) are shown in landscaped areas with tree canopies. No dimension callouts verify that these locations are within 6 feet of drivable surfaces. The eastern transformer locations appear to be separated from the main parking/driveway circulation by buildings and landscaping. Without explicit dimension callouts or clear site plan notation showing 6-foot accessibility, compliance cannot be verified. This represents genuine ambiguity rather than clear non-compliance.

findings.comment: 24/7 truck access to transformer locations not provided, shown on plans, or is obstructed by site improvements, fencing, or other features. Transformer pad locations are shown but access design is incomplete (noted as 'need to look up approp. detail'). No dimensioned access route from parking areas is provided, and distances from transformer pads to drivable surfaces are not verified. Provide detailed access plans for each transformer pad showing: (1) dimensioned distance from each pad to adjacent parking/traffic surfaces (must be within 6 feet), (2) surface specifications for access routes (HMAC or PCC pavement capable of supporting bucket truck weight), and (3) complete transformer pad detail that confirms truck accessibility for installation, operation, and maintenance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations on west and east sides of the site
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and Site Plan (Sheet 9) confirms: (1) Two pad-mounted transformer pads are clearly labeled and shown on the plans—one on the west side of the site south of Bldg. 1 and west of Bldg. 2, and one on the east side between Bldg. 5 and Bldg. 6. (2) A note on the electrical plan adjacent to the transformer pad reads exactly: 'need to look up approp. detail,' indicating the design is incomplete. (3) Vision analysis explicitly states: 'There is NO dimensioned access route explicitly drawn or labeled from the parking areas or public ROW to either transformer location.' (4) The analysis notes: 'Both transformers are sited immediately adjacent (visually within a few feet) to the internal drivable surface/parking aisle curbs. Exact distance dimensions from the curb to the pads are not provided.' (5) No dimensions are shown from parking areas or driveways to the transformer pads, and no specification confirms they are within 6 feet of drivable surfaces.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires 'Truck access to AE Construction and Existing Facility Sites' and specifies that 'Equipment pads: Within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility.' UCM § 1.10.4 addresses 'Clearances from AE Padmount Equipment' and includes the requirement that transformer pads must have truck accessibility. The regulatory overview states 'Equipment pads: Within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck accessibility.' The site plan must provide dimensioned evidence that each transformer pad is within 6 feet of a parking area or traffic surface capable of supporting bucket trucks. The incomplete detail notation ('need to look up approp. detail') and the absence of dimensions confirming the 6-foot proximity requirement constitute deficiencies. The applicant must provide specific dimensional verification of truck access to each pad.

findings.comment: Distance from transformer pads to nearest drivable surface not dimensionally verified on plans. Provide dimensioned measurements from each transformer pad to the nearest drivable surface, confirming either that pads are within 6 feet of drivable surface, or alternatively that 20-foot all-weather access routes are provided where pads exceed 6 feet from drivable surfaces.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads appear to be within approximately 6 feet of drivable surfaces based on visual scale assessment (1" = 20'). The pads are shown as rectangular symbols in landscaped islands immediately adjacent to paved driveways. However, no specific dimension lines or measurements are labeled on the plans to confirm the exact distance from each pad to the nearest drivable surface. If any transformers are more than 6 feet from a drivable surface, a 20-foot all-weather access route would be required, but no such access routes are explicitly shown or called out on the plans.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformers to be either: (1) within 6 feet of a drivable surface with standard access, or (2) if more than 6 feet away, served by a 20-foot all-weather access route. The plans do not dimensionally verify the distances from each transformer pad to the drivable surface. While visual inspection suggests all pads are close to driveways, without explicit measurements, it cannot be confirmed that all pads meet this requirement or that adequate access routes are provided. The preliminary nature of the electrical plan means precise distances may not be finalized.

findings.comment: Transformer pad 2 is located directly adjacent to parking with less than 2 feet of clearance. Site plan does not show a dedicated 20-foot all-weather truck access route for this transformer. Provide either: (1) a documented dedicated truck access easement at least 20 feet long to the transformer pad, or (2) demonstrated coordination with Austin Energy confirming the parking lot access is acceptable for transformer truck operations.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5)
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 and Sheet 9 to identify transformer locations and proximity to parking/traffic areas. Transformer 2, located on the eastern side between Bldg. 4 and 5, is positioned directly adjacent to a surface parking space with less than 2 feet of separation. The vision analysis confirmed this transformer sits within a few inches of the nearest parking space. No 20-foot all-weather access route is shown extending from the transformer pad to provide alternative access if the 6-foot threshold is exceeded. Access to this transformer depends entirely on proximity to the main paved driveway loop with no separate dedicated truck access route.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require transformer pads to be located within 6 feet of a drivable surface or parking/traffic area, OR if greater than 6 feet away, a 20-foot all-weather access route must be provided. Transformer 2 is clearly within 6 feet of parking (approximately 2 feet), which meets the first condition. However, the vision analysis of Sheet 9 indicates the transformer is located in a confined landscape island between parking and the driveway with no separate access easement or dedicated truck route. The requirement implies that Austin Energy trucks must have direct, unobstructed access to reach the transformer pad. The current configuration shows the pad accessible only via parking lot navigation or via the main driveway, neither of which is documented as a dedicated access route. While the distance technically satisfies the 6-foot requirement, the lack of any dedicated access documentation and the tight confinement of the pad suggest the intent of the requirement (to ensure reliable truck access) may not be met.

findings.comment: 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance not dimensionally verified on plans. Provide dimensioned site plan details showing the 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area in front of each transformer pad, with clearance to buildings, structures, and other obstructions, and confirm 35-foot vertical clearance above each pad is maintained.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21. Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads, and Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad location in a landscaped island. However, no dimensions or clearance zones are labeled on either sheet. The 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance is not dimensionally shown or verified on any plan. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations, so the vertical clearance above the pads cannot be verified. The site has extensive retaining walls and grade changes up to 9+ feet, creating constrained spaces. Without dimensional verification of the set-up area and vertical clearance, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.reasoning: Code requires a minimum 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area in front of transformer equipment with 35-foot vertical clearance above. The site plans do not dimensionally verify that this area is provided at each transformer location. The site's constrained layout with retaining walls and significant grade changes makes this requirement difficult to verify without explicit dimensioning. The set-up area must be maintained clear of obstructions. Without plan annotations confirming the set-up area dimensions and vertical clearance at each transformer location, compliance is unclear.

findings.comment: Transformer pads lack required clear zone: 20-foot × 35-foot set-up area in front of transformer equipment not maintained. Trees and tree wells immediately adjacent to transformer pads obstruct required vertical clearance and set-up depth.
applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations (west side near Buildings 1/8, and two on east side near Buildings 4 and 6)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows three transformer pads with scale 1" = 20'. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies one transformer pad adjacent to a 'Tree Well' with tree symbol immediately north (within 2-5 feet). Vision analysis of Sheet 21 revealed large circular tree canopy symbols overlapping or adjacent to all three transformer pad locations. Sheet 9 site plan shows internal driveway widths ranging from 21.3' to 29.6' with parking stalls immediately adjacent to transformer pad. No plan sheets depict or dimension a 20' × 35' set-up area in front of any transformer pad, nor do they show 35-foot vertical clearances above the pads. Tree wells and tree canopies shown on both electrical plan and site plan would obstruct the required set-up area and vertical clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 20' × 35' set-up area in front of transformer equipment with 35-foot vertical clearance. The project plans show transformer pads with trees (canopy symbols and tree wells) immediately adjacent, obstructing the required set-up area dimensions and vertical clearance. No alternative notation of approved reduced clearances or AE Design variance is documented. The physical constraints of tree placement, building proximity, and parking layout make the required set-up area unachievable without relocating trees or redesigning the site layout.

findings.comment: Transformer pad 1 is directly adjacent to a tree well, which obstructs access and creates a site feature blocking the required clear zone around the transformer. Remove the tree well or relocate the transformer to a site location that is free of landscaping, trees, tree wells, and other obstructions within a minimum 20 ft × 35 ft clear set-up area. Alternatively, provide documented coordination with Austin Energy Design and the arborist confirming the tree well can be modified or removed to provide unobstructed transformer access.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad 1 (western edge, adjacent to Bldg. 2)
Tree well and landscaping area near Transformer 1
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21 to identify site features near transformer pads. Transformer 1, located on the far western edge north of the main entrance driveway, is positioned directly adjacent to a labeled 'Tree Well' on Sheet 9. Vision analysis confirmed this transformer pad 'directly abuts a labeled Tree Well to its north.' Tree wells are protective structures around tree trunks that prevent direct vehicle access and movement. Additional overlapping tree canopy symbols were noted on Sheet 21 in the vicinity of T1. The transformer pad is surrounded by landscape elements that would restrict truck maneuvering and equipment placement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require that transformer pads 'be kept clear of all structures, landscaping, and improvements' to ensure Austin Energy personnel can install, operate, and maintain equipment with appropriate vehicle and personnel access. 'Trees, landscaping, street furniture, dumpster enclosures, water meters, grates, poles, fire hydrants' and other obstructions cannot block access to transformer pads or create safety hazards during equipment servicing. A tree well directly adjacent to the transformer pad represents a site feature that physically obstructs the clear zone and restricts the space available for truck approach, equipment landing, and personnel movement. Tree wells are designed to limit access to protect tree roots; this directly conflicts with the unrestricted access requirement for electrical equipment.

findings.comment: Site features (trees, landscaping in tree wells) blocking access to transformer pads. Transformer pads not kept clear of all structures and landscaping for Austin Energy 24/7 access.
applicableAreas: All three transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) vision analysis identified large circular tree canopy symbols overlapping or immediately adjacent to all three transformer pad locations. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies a 'Tree Well' with tree symbol immediately adjacent (within 2-5 feet) to the westernmost transformer pad. Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) shows extensive tree planting with designations for street yard trees (SY), parking lot trees (PL), and mitigation trees (M), but does not exclude trees from transformer access zones. No notation on any sheet indicates trees are excluded from transformer pad clearance zones or set-up areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require transformer pads to be kept clear of all structures and landscaping to ensure Austin Energy 24/7 access. Trees are explicitly prohibited from transformer access zones and set-up areas due to interference with truck access, visual sight lines, root zone conflicts with subsurface infrastructure, and safety concerns. The presence of tree canopies and tree wells immediately adjacent to transformer pads (as shown on Sheets 21 and 9) creates obstructions that violate the requirement for unobstructed access and set-up area.

findings.comment: Landscape plans do not demonstrate that landscaping avoids required staging areas adjacent to transformer locations. Please: (1) show all transformer pad locations and their 20' × 35' staging areas (with 35' vertical clearance) on the landscape plan; (2) add note stating no landscaping (trees, shrubs, hardscape) is permitted within these clear zones; (3) provide detail showing how existing landscaping plan respects transformer access requirements.
applicableAreas: Areas adjacent to transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show these transformer pads. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because the electric transformers and their associated required clearance/staging zones are not drawn on this sheet, it is impossible to determine from this document alone if landscaping elements conflict with those specific staging areas.' Cannot verify whether landscaping (trees, shrubs, hardscape, irrigation) is placed within the required 20' × 35' clear zone with 35' vertical clearance in front of transformer access doors.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 specifies that pad-mounted transformers require 'Minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal clear zone with 35 feet vertical clearance in front of pad-mounted transformers, vaults, and other AE equipment requiring crane/bucket truck access for installation and maintenance.' The landscape plan must show these clearance zones and must not include landscaping within them. Since Sheet 31 does not show the transformer pads, coordination cannot be verified. Without explicit depiction of staging areas and exclusion of landscaping, compliance cannot be determined.

findings.comment: No setup areas (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal) are shown in front of any of the four transformer pads. Design must designate and dimension the required crane/bucket truck access space for each piece of AE equipment per UCM § 1.3.16.
applicableAreas: Equipment setups in front of four transformer pads
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts four transformer pads (blue rectangles labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad') at four locations: west of Building 1/2, between Buildings 4 and 5, between Buildings 6 and 7, and west of Building 8. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the same equipment locations in context of buildings, parking, driveways, and sidewalks. However, neither sheet shows any delineated setup area in front of the transformers. No dashed lines, dimensions, or text labels indicating a 20-foot × 35-foot setup area (or any alternative dimensions) were found on either the electrical plan or site plan sheets. The transformer locations are shown graphically but the required horizontal space for truck/crane access is not designated.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 20 feet × 35 feet horizontal space in front of all AE equipment for crane and bucket truck access. The applicant has not designated or dimensioned this required space on the site plan or electrical plan. While the equipment locations are shown, the absence of a clearly marked and dimensioned setup area means compliance with this clearance requirement cannot be verified. The preliminary design stage does not exempt the applicant from showing how this mandatory clearance will be provided.

findings.comment: No vertical clearance (minimum 35 feet) is shown or verified above any transformer pad. Building elevations are required to demonstrate adequate clearance for crane/bucket truck access, or alternative equipment locations must be provided.
applicableAreas: Vertical clearance space above equipment setups
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations but does not indicate any vertical clearance envelope or dimension. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows building heights ranging from 33'−4.75" to 36'−1". However, no indication is provided of the vertical clearance above each transformer, such as overhead obstructions (canopies, overhanging structures, tree branches, or overhead utility lines). The preliminary electrical design shows no analysis of vertical clearance above the equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 35 feet vertical clearance in front of AE equipment for crane/bucket truck access. Without building elevations or vertical clearance analysis, there is no evidence that 35 feet of vertical clearance is (or will be) available at each equipment location. The presence of buildings with 33−36 foot heights in proximity to the transformers raises questions about whether adequate clearance exists, but this cannot be verified without elevations.

findings.comment: No truck access path (minimum 12 feet width, 16 feet vertical clearance) is designated or dimensioned on site plan or electrical plan. Design must identify the truck access route(s) to all AE equipment and dimension them to verify compliance with UCM § 1.3.16 standards, including surface load rating specifications.
applicableAreas: Access paths to transformer pads and electrical equipment throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows internal driveways, parking areas, and pedestrian circulation. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pad and pull box locations. However, neither sheet designates or dimensions a specific truck access path to the on-site electric facilities. No path is labeled with minimum 12 feet horizontal width or 16 feet vertical clearance specifications. While driveways exist on the site, there is no explicit confirmation that they will be maintained to support AE truck access to equipment, nor are the paths dimensioned to verify compliance with minimum width and clearance standards.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires a minimum 12 feet horizontal width and 16 feet vertical clearance for truck access to AE facilities, with surfaces capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight). The applicant must explicitly designate, dimension, and label the truck access path(s) on the site plan and verify they meet these standards. Absence of documented access paths means the applicant has not demonstrated compliance with this mandatory requirement.

findings.comment: Horizontal width of truck access paths to transformer pads not dimensionally verified. Provide dimensioned site plan showing minimum 12-foot width access route from drivable surface to each transformer pad, measured at the narrowest point of the access path.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad access routes
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. All four transformer pads are shown adjacent to paved internal driveways. The 1" = 20' scale plan shows the pads in proximity to driveways, but no specific width dimensions are labeled for the access routes to the transformer pads. Sheet 9 shows driveway details referencing "Construct Type III Driveway See Detail 433S-2", but transformer-specific access route width requirements are not explicitly dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 12-foot horizontal width for truck access paths to transformer pads. While the plans show transformer pads adjacent to driveways, the width of the access path from the drivable surface to the transformer pad is not dimensionally verified. Typical internal site driveways may be 12-20 feet wide overall, but the specific access route to each transformer pad must meet the 12-foot minimum. Without dimensional verification at the transformer pad locations, compliance is unclear.

findings.comment: Vertical clearance of truck access paths to transformer pads not verified. Provide grading plan or building section details showing transformer pad locations with spot elevations, and verify that minimum 16-foot vertical clearance is maintained along all access routes to transformer pads, including clearances from building eaves, overhangs, and any other overhead structures.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad access routes
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows extensive contour lines and spot elevations across the site, indicating significant grade changes (9+ feet total elevation change across site). However, transformer pad locations are NOT shown on the grading plan. Building Finished Floor Elevations (FFE) are provided but transformer pad elevations are not. Without transformer pad elevations and spot elevations along the access routes, the vertical clearances and access route slopes cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Code requires minimum 16-foot vertical clearance for truck access paths to transformer pads. This clearance must be verified by checking building heights, overhead structures, and any other obstructions above the access route. The grading plan does not show transformer pad locations or their associated vertical clearance zones. Without this information, it is impossible to verify that 16-foot vertical clearance is maintained along all access paths. Any overhead structures, eaves, awnings, or other features crossing above the access routes would need to be checked against this requirement.

findings.comment: Transformer pad access surfaces not specified as hot mix asphaltic concrete (HMAC) or Portland cement concrete (PCC) pavement. Provide detailed construction specifications and engineering calculations confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces meet all-weather pavement requirements and load capacity standards.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) which show four transformer pad locations adjacent to driveways. Transformer pads are drawn as rectangular symbols within landscaped islands adjacent to paved access routes. No specifications or annotations are provided on any sheet indicating the surface material of the transformer pad access areas. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad in a landscaped/unpaved island area between a sidewalk and drive aisle. No notes or details specify that access surfaces are HMAC or PCC pavement, nor are any structural specifications or load capacity information provided.
findings.reasoning: Code requires transformer pad access surfaces to be all-weather prepared surfaces (HMAC or PCC pavement). UCM § 1.3.16 and LDC § 25-12-173 establish that access surfaces must be hot mix asphaltic concrete or Portland cement concrete pavement capable of supporting required vehicle weight. The site plan shows transformer pads in landscaped areas adjacent to driveways but does not confirm the pad access surfaces themselves are prepared pavement. Gravel, grass, or unpaved surfaces do not meet this requirement. Without explicit specification and detail of the transformer pad access surface material as HMAC or PCC with adequate structural design, compliance cannot be verified. The preliminary electrical plan does not include construction details or material specifications for transformer pad surfaces.

findings.comment: Structural capacity of transformer pad access surfaces not documented. Provide pavement design calculations and structural engineering certification confirming that all transformer pad access surfaces can support 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight (32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight) without damage.
applicableAreas: All four transformer pad locations on electrical plan
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21 for access surface design and load capacity documentation. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows spot elevations and contour lines across the site but does NOT show transformer pad locations or elevations. Sheets 9 and 21 show four transformer pads adjacent to paved driveways but provide no pavement design calculations, structural details, or load capacity specifications. No engineering calculations or structural design documentation is visible on any sheet confirming the access surfaces can support the required 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with maximum 32,530 lbs rear axle weight.
findings.reasoning: Code requires access surfaces to be capable of supporting 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with 32,530 lbs maximum rear axle weight without damage. This requires structural design calculations appropriate to soil conditions and pavement type. The site plan and grading plan do not show transformer pad locations with associated structural details or pavement design calculations. Without structural calculations specific to each transformer pad location, it cannot be verified that the access surfaces meet load capacity requirements. The burden is on the applicant to demonstrate compliance through engineering design.

findings.comment: Adequate set-up area and clearances at transformer equipment not documented, and AE Design approval of any deviations not shown. Provide either (1) dimensioned plans confirming 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance at all transformers, or (2) documented AE Design written approval of specific project deviations with approval conditions clearly noted on plans.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21. Neither sheet provides dimensioned set-up areas, vertical clearance measurements, or AE Design approval documentation for the transformer equipment. Sheet 9 shows one typical transformer pad in a landscaped island adjacent to a driveway and sidewalk area. The constrained site layout with retaining walls and limited maneuvering space suggests that the standard 20 ft × 35 ft set-up area with 35-foot vertical clearance may be difficult to achieve without deviations. No AE Design approval documentation is visible on the plans authorizing any reduced clearances or alternative configurations.
findings.reasoning: Code allows for AE Design-approved deviations from standard set-up area and clearance requirements. However, any such deviations require documented AE Design approval with specific conditions. The preliminary plans show no evidence of such approval. Without either confirmation of standard set-up areas and clearances, or documented AE Design approval of deviations, compliance cannot be verified. The site's constrained layout strongly suggests that deviations from standard requirements may be necessary, but these must be explicitly approved and documented.

findings.comment: AE vehicle turnaround or exit capability not provided. Revise site plan to provide a turnaround area (hammerhead, T-turn, or cul-de-sac) at the eastern drive aisle terminus with minimum dimensions per UCM § 1.3.16 (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet set-up area with 35 feet vertical clearance for AE vehicles). Show AE truck access routing and confirm turn-around capability.
applicableAreas: Eastern drive aisle terminus
Dead-end access for emergency and utility vehicles
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows internal drive aisles with two permanent driveway entrances on the western property line. The eastern drive aisle extends into the site to service Buildings 3-6 but terminates in a dead-end configuration at a curb and gutter line with a retaining wall beyond. No labeled or graphically defined turnaround area (hammerhead, T-turn, cul-de-sac, or other turning radius) is shown for vehicles to turn around or exit. The sheet provides no information about AE truck access requirements or vehicle turnaround capability.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that all AE facilities have truck access with the ability to turn around or exit the property. The site has four transformer pads (shown on Sheet 21) that require periodic maintenance and service access by Austin Energy vehicles. The dead-end eastern drive aisle does not provide the AE vehicles with ability to turn around or exit efficiently. This violates the truck access turnaround requirement.
